scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Caci originated as a harvest ritual among the Manggarai people of Flores island, Indonesia.
It is indigenous to the Lesser Sunda Islands and has been practiced historically as a form of dispute settlement between villages.
The ritual is linked to a local legend about two brothers and a buffalo, celebrated with caci matches.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Caci is performed mainly during traditional harvest festivals like Penti, held every five years, and the Karong Woja Wole festival among the Ndolu ethnic group.
It marks the end of the harvest and the start of a new crop cycle.
The ritual serves as both a competitive sport and a sacrificial offering to ancestors for fertility and good harvests.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Caci is performed by two bare-chested male fighters wearing pants covered by embroidered songket sarongs, jingling bells on their lower backs and ankles, and horned buffalo-hide helmets.
Fighters alternate roles as attacker and defender.
The attacker delivers up to three blows with a whip or stick, aiming primarily for the opponent’s head or face, while the defender blocks with a shield.
Watch for Whip Spin, Three-strike Attack.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music accompanying caci fights is performed by women who play drums and gongs.
The rhythmic beating supports the fighters’ movements and energizes the crowd.
Listen for the drums, gongs, jingling bells.
The music features rhythmic drum and gong beats supporting the duel’s tempo, punctuated by the jingling bells worn by fighters, creating a lively and tense atmosphere.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Fighters wear pants covered by embroidered woven songket sarongs, small jingling bells on their lower backs and ankles, and horned helmets made of buffalo hide wrapped in colorful cloths.
The helmets protect the face and head, which are the primary targets.
The shield is round or elliptical, made from buffalo hide or wood, and traditionally undecorated.

scenes.title: The people
narration: In Manggarai Regency, both whip and stick forms of caci exist, though the stick form is now rare.
Caci is a martial art indigenous to the Lesser Sunda Islands and part of the Manggarai cultural heritage.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Caci is sibling of Pencak Silat: Both are Indonesian martial arts with ritual and combat elements.
Caci is sibling of Perang Pandan: Another Indonesian ritual stick fighting tradition.
Caci is sibling of Cakalele: Maluku warrior dance involving weapons.
Caci is sibling of Kabasaran: Minahasa war dance with weaponry.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Caci has a sacrificial function; blood from wounds is offered to ancestors to ensure soil fertility and a good harvest. The ritual is traditionally connected to harvest ceremonies and is not merely a sport or dance.

The helmets protect the face and head, which are the primary targets. The shield is round or elliptical, made from buffalo hide or wood, and traditionally undecorated. Matches take place in the yard of a communal house or a village arena, often during festivals such as Penti or Karong Woja Wole.
visual_brief.setting_notes: Caci is performed mainly during traditional harvest festivals like Penti, held every five years, and the Karong Woja Wole festival among the Ndolu ethnic group. It marks the end of the harvest and the start of a new crop cycle. The ritual serves as both a competitive sport and a sacrificial offering to ancestors for fertility and good harvests. Historically, it also functioned as a dispute resolution method between villages. Today, it attracts tourists and serves as a cultural identity marker for the Manggarai people.
